messages:
Elena Torres: Heads-up - Nimbus Logistics POC keeps getting 403s on /v1/embeddings. They can authenticate (200 for /v1/health) but embedding calls fail with 'insufficient scope' or 'project not found'. Seen across two regions.
Devon Park: can you paste the failing request (headers + body redacted)?
Elena Torres: here's a sanitized snippet from their harness:
```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.prod
Authorization: Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1Qi...
X-Project: nimbus-poc
Content-Type: application/json

{"model":"rwd-small-embed","input":["order 12345"]}
```
Response: 403 {"error":"project not found or insufficient permissions"} + header `x-rate-hint: quota-exhausted` sometimes.
Chris R.: hmm `X-Project` header isn't an allowed auth signal anymore, we require org/project in JWT claims or the x-org/project headers that are behind our trusted proxy. Are they using a shadow key or service account token?
Elena Torres: they said they created a service principal with scope `embeddings.read` and bound it to project via the console. We validated the console binding shows `nimbus-poc`.
Devon Park: ask them to dump the JWT claims (sub, org, project, scopes, exp). Could be the token issuer set `project` claim at `project_id` instead of `project`. We had a mismatch earlier where the claim name differed.
Elena Torres: they shared claims: `{"sub":"svc-nimbus","org":"nimbus","project_id":"nimbus-poc","scopes":["embeddings:read"]}` — aha. project_id vs project.
presales-bot: Tip: tokens must include `project` claim or use the `x-project` header injected by a trusted proxy. Console mappings may accept `project_id` but API validation is strict.
infra-oncall: I can add a compatibility layer to accept `project_id` for a short window, but prefer fix on customer's token issuer. We can also return a more helpful error: `missing project claim 'project'`.
Chris R.: another possibility: their token scope is `embeddings:read` but API expects `embeddings` or `embeddings.*` depending on config. Could be scope name normalization.
Elena Torres: they just tried swapping scope to `embeddings` and redeployed — still 403.
Devon Park: okay next check: ensure the org in token matches the org on the project. If token org is `nimbus` but project is under `nimbus-corp`, that will also 403. Ask for `org` claim exact value.
Elena Torres: they confirmed `org":"nimbus"` and project in console is `nimbus-poc` under org `nimbus` — matches.
infra-oncall: I ran a quick trace from our authz service for their token fingerprint. Looks like authz failed at claim normalization: codepath expecting `project` claim, not `project_id`. I'll push a short-lived form-compat patch to validate both. Deploying to staging now.
Elena Torres: while you do that, customer asked about rate limits because they saw `x-rate-hint: quota-exhausted`. Is that from our side or their account quota?
Devon Park: that header is emitted when token passes authz but project has no remaining embedding units in the reserved quota. Could be they used up free trial credits. Presales: Elena, can you confirm what plan they signed up for and whether they reached quota?
presales-bot: Reminder: POC intake checklist: collect plan, quota, service-account type, token issuer, proxy in front. :memo:
Elena Torres: Nimbus says they signed up on the Starter trial (100k embedding units). They ran a bulk import earlier which might have consumed credits. They'll check.
infra-oncall: staging patch applied. I also added a diagnostic endpoint that returns parsed claims we see server-side (only accessible from their IP). Ask them to hit `/internal/debug/claims` and paste result.
Chris R.: also tell them to avoid sending `X-Project` from their CI runners — it can be stripped by some runners or overwritten. Best practice: assert claims are present in JWT.
Elena Torres: they hit the debug endpoint, response shows `project: null`, `project_id: "nimbus-poc"`, `scopes: ["embeddings"]`. So patch helped us see the mismatch. They updated token generator to set `project` claim and re-issued tokens.
Devon Park: after reissue, did embeddings succeed?
Elena Torres: yes — immediate success and no more 403s. They also confirmed the bulk import exhausted trial credits earlier; presales flagged a conversion conversation.
presales-bot: Suggestion: offer a short-term embed quota top-up for POC conversions to help demo at scale. :moneybag:
Chris R.: I'll follow up with infra to remove the compatibility tolerance in 72h and add clearer error text in the API: `403 missing project claim 'project' or insufficient scope`.
Elena Torres: I'll document the troubleshooting steps in the POC ticket: 1) verify token claims (project vs project_id), 2) check scope naming, 3) confirm org/project binding in Console, 4) verify quota via billing UI. Linking ticket after standup. Thanks all :rocket:
